Context:
- `knowledge-base/DECISIONS.md` (decisions taken, and why)
- `GOAL.md` (the goal of the project (long-term direction, scope, non-scope, ...))
- `BUSINESS_LOGIC.md` (codebase business logic)
- `knowledge-base/FACTS.md` (non-obvious facts relevant to the project)
- `knowledge-base/INSIGHTS.md` (insights relevant to the project)
- `knowledge-base/MARKET_RESEARCH.md` (the market the project competes in)
- `knowledge-base/**.md` (more files holding knowledge related to the project)
- `tickets/**.md` (things to potentially work on; format: the "Ticketing format" section below)
- `.the-framework/conversations/**.md` (conversations between humans, recorded by agents (e.g. the agent Discord bot))
- `TODO_AGENTS.md` (the AI task queue; format: the "TODO_AGENTS.md" section below)

# Ticketing format


## tickets/<DATE>_<SLUG>.md

DATE: yyyy-mm-dd
SLUG: succinct kebab-case slug of the ticket title
Body:
```md
Priority: 0-10 [optional, 10: critical — act immediately, 0: only if capacity]
Topics: [list-of-topics] [optional]
GitHub: [#42](https://github.com/org/repo/issues/42) [optional]

# Ticket title

## TLDR

...

## Why it matters

...

[optional: more info (any heading and format you want)]
```

When a ticket is closed, it should be removed from the repository (also its `.plan.md` and `.lock.md`), so that `tickets/*` only contains open tickets.


## tickets/<DATE>_<SLUG>.lock.md

Body:
```md
CLAIMED: <SESSION_ID> (<SESSION_NAME>)
```

Whenever an agent is working/planning a ticket, a `.lock.md` file must be created to avoid two agents working/planning the same ticket.


## tickets/<DATE>_<SLUG>.plan.md

For an existing ticket (e.g. `tickets/2042-01-01_some-ticket.md`), a plan can be created (`tickets/2042-01-01_some-ticket.plan.md`).

Body:
```md
Effort: 0-10 [0: implementation is trivial, 10: implementation takes months]
Uncertainty: 0-10 [0: implementation without meaningful alternatives, 10: highly uncertain how to implement]
Outdated: yes [optional, only if the ticket was updated in a way that makes the plan outdated]

# [Plan] Ticket title

Single-sentence describing this file's content.

## TLDR [optional]

Brief overiew of this file's content.

## Problems [optional]

List of all significant aspects with low confidence on how to implement, with explanation why uncertain.

## Solutions [optional]

For each problem, list of ways to solve the problem (including meaningful shortcuts, for quicker implementation).

## Considerations [optional]

Exhaustive list of all significant aspects to be considered (including edge cases).

## Implementation [optional]

Concrete plan to implement the ticket.
```

Notes:
- Covers both spiking (e.g. high-level research without implementation plan) and planning (e.g. concrete implementation proposal)
- The `.plan.md` file can be modified multiple times over an extended period (e.g. a ticket requiring repeated human intervention, transitioning from spiking to concrete plan)
- All sections are just proposals and optional: you can use any headings with any format
- The uncertainty value:
  - Gauges whether there are *significant* alternatives, minor variability such as syntax should be ignored
  - Is used for evaluating whether human intervention is needed (0 => clearly no human intervention needed)
- Example of how to gauge uncertainty and alternatives:
  - List all aspects that need to be considered
  - Give an uncertainty rating (0-10) to each aspect following this criteria: is there an obviously optimal way to implement it (0), or is it highly unclear whether it can be implemented in a better way (10)?
  - Explore and suggest alternatives for each aspect with a low rating

# TODO_AGENTS.md

Content:
```md
## Priority 10 (critical — act immediately)

...

## Priority 9

- [Succinct description](/link-for-more-details)
- Or self-contained TODO item with complete description of what should be done

...

## Priority 0 (only if capacity)

...
```

The TODO_AGENTS.md file lists *all* tasks AI will work on next, sorted by priority.

To remove an item (e.g. when done), simply remove it from `TODO_AGENTS.md`.

Priority 10 is rarely used (e.g. critical production bugs) and should be treated as utmost priority.

Within a priority, the first tasks have higher priority (they're the "next" tasks within that "priortiy queue").

# System prompt

SHOW_MD: Show it via `showMarkdown()`
SHOW_CHOICES: Show it via `showChoices()`
AWAIT: Stop, await user answer before resuming
SESSION_NAME: the name of the session
TODO_FILE: `TODO_AGENTS.md`
ADD_ANALYSIS_ENTRY: Add entry to the ANALYSIS_RESULT.md list

## Analyze the user prompt

Analyze the user prompt, follow the instructions, create ANALYSIS_RESULT.md that lists the analysis results, and show it via showMarkdownSecondary()

### Ambiguous prompt

If it isn't clear what you should do (e.g. unclear scope, unclear user prompt), make a list of interpretations sorted by plausibility, <SHOW_CHOICES>, <AWAIT>

<ADD_ANALYSIS_ENTRY> whether YES/NO the prompt is ambiguous

### Scope

- If the scope of what you'll work on is *large*, create a `PLAN_<SESSION_NAME>.agent.md` of what you'll work on, <SHOW_MD>, <AWAIT>
- If the scope is potentially *very large* (e.g. spans over many hours/days of work), consider adding entries to <TODO_FILE> (backlog of follow-up tasks) and show new entries <SHOW_MD>

<ADD_ANALYSIS_ENTRY> whether the scope is small, large, or very large


## Before starting changes

Do the following before applying your first change.

### Session name

1. Create a <SESSION_NAME> as a string [a-z0-9-]+ that succinctly represents the intention of the user prompt
2. Create a new branch `the-framework/<SESSION_NAME>` and `$ git checkout` it — do all the work in that branch
3. Call setSessionName(<SESSION_NAME>)


## Before applying changes

Do the following before applying changes — do it again anytime you make new changes.

### Alternatives

Measure "variability":
- List all high-level problems that you're about to solve
- Give a rating to each problem (from 0 to 10) following this criteria: is there an obviously optimal way to solve the problem (10), or is it highly unclear whether the problem can be solved in a better way (0)?
- Explore and suggest alternatives for problems with a low rating
- For each problem that has alternatives: list all alternatives sorted in a sensible order, <SHOW_CHOICES>, <AWAIT>


## After applying changes

After you're done, decide: is <SESSION_NAME> finished, with no work left to do?
- Yes: call setReadyForMerge() — required, the work is never merged without it
- No: don't call it; say what's left instead

## Awaiting a choice
When these instructions tell you to showChoices() / showMultiSelect() / showMarkdown() and then AWAIT, do not decide for the user.
End your turn with one fenced code block, then stop.
For a single choice (showChoices, pick one), tag it `await-choices`:
```await-choices
{ "title": "<the question>", "options": [{ "label": "<option>", "detail": "<optional one-liner>" }], "recommended": "<the label to default to>" }
```
For a multi-select (showMultiSelect, pick any number), tag it `await-multiselect` and set `default` on the entries that start checked:
```await-multiselect
{ "title": "<the prompt>", "options": [{ "label": "<option>", "detail": "<optional one-liner>", "default": true }] }
```
For a plan/document approval (showMarkdown of a file you wrote, then AWAIT), tag it `await-confirmation` and name the file:
```await-confirmation
{ "title": "<what to approve>", "file": "PLAN_<slug>.agent.md" }
```
The framework shows it, waits for the user, and re-prompts you with their answer. Do not continue past it on your own.

## Handing the browser to a human
When you are working in a browser and hit something you cannot or should not get past yourself — a login wall, a captcha, an SSO or 2FA step — stop and hand it over. Never type a password, never attempt a captcha, and never use a credential you found lying around in the repo or the environment. Tag the block `await-browser`:
```await-browser
{ "title": "<what the human needs to do>", "url": "<the page you are stuck on>" }
```
The user acts in that browser, then you are re-prompted. Their answer says whether it was handled: if it was not, do not retry the same page — say what you could not reach and work on what you can, or stop. Use this only for the browser; a decision the user needs to make is `await-choices`.

## Showing a document without waiting
To display markdown in the side panel without blocking (a plan, a summary, a writeup) and keep working, put a `show-markdown` block anywhere in your turn. The first line is its title:
```show-markdown
# <title>
<the markdown body>
```
This just shows it; you do not stop. Re-emit the same title to update that view in place.
showMarkdown() and showMarkdownSecondary() are both this block: emit the same `show-markdown` block for either.

## Session name
When you call setSessionName(<name>) (after creating and checking out the `the-framework/<name>` branch), also emit a `set-session-name` block naming it, so the dashboard shows which session this is. The first non-empty line is the name (a `[a-z0-9-]` slug):
```set-session-name
<name>
```
You do not stop; re-emit it if you rename the session.

## Ready for merge
When you call setReadyForMerge() — you believe the work is complete and ready for human review — emit an empty `ready-for-merge` block. This flips the dashboard status from building to ready; it does not stop your turn.
```ready-for-merge
```

event.text: I'll start by reading the ticket and getting oriented.
There's an existing plan file for this ticket and no lock file. Let me read the plan.
`AGENTS.md` confirms the zero-users / clean-code policy the plan relies on. Now reading the remaining affected files.
The generator derives constant names from filenames (`presets/plan_tickets.md` → `PRESETS_PLAN_TICKETS`), so renaming the file is sufficient. Now the remaining UI copy and tests.
The registry only covers quality presets — no change needed there. Now the catalog:
Now `auto-pm.ts` — identifiers, strings, and the comments that name them:
Core sources done. Now the UI copy, website, and docs:
All product surfaces are renamed. Now the tests — starting with the two big ones:
Now the `spike-1-0` lock-id fixtures across the remaining test files:

The ticket is done. All tests pass (1690/1690 in `the-framework`, 81/81 test files in `framework-dashboard`, 21/21 turbo tasks), the sweep is committed as `9feab2d`, and the ticket, its plan, its lock, and its queue entry are removed.

```set-session-name
avoid-term-spike
```

```show-markdown
# ANALYSIS_RESULT
- **Ambiguous prompt:** NO — the prompt pins one ticket (`tickets/2026-07-31_avoid-term-spike.md`) and forbids starting others. The ticket has a committed plan (`Effort: 2, Uncertainty: 1`) with concrete per-site replacements and pre-made decisions.
- **Scope:** small — a wording/identifier rename sweep across ~20 files plus test updates; single session, no `PLAN_*.agent.md` needed.
- **Plan drift:** the plan is from 2026-07-31; the code moved. Two plan sites no longer exist (`ticketing_format.md` no longer says "spiking"), and new "spike" sites appeared (`spec.md`, `TicketsPanel.tsx`, new test fixtures). The plan's own vocabulary rules extended to them mechanically — no new decisions required.
- **Variability:** all decisions were pre-made in the committed plan (replacement vocabulary; renaming identifiers including the persisted preset id, per `AGENTS.md` zero-users policy). No problem rated low enough to require presenting alternatives.
- **Autonomy:** the ticket explicitly asks to be executed autonomously (dogfooding #1334) — proceeded without AWAIT.
```

## What changed

**User-facing wording** (the ticket's core):
- The routine is now labeled **"Plan tickets (aka spike)"** — the ticket's own suggested name — and its status line reads `planning "<ticket>"` instead of `spiking & planning "<ticket>"`.
- The rotation's idle note is now "every open ticket already has a plan, or an agent on the way to one"; the pinned fan-out prompt says "plan exactly one ticket".
- Fan-out agent ids (visible in `.lock.md` claims and on ticket detail pages) are `plan-<t>-<i>` instead of `spike-<t>-<i>`.
- Onboarding copy → "The agent researches and plans them"; website → "Research, plan, and prioritize your tickets"; `spec.md` → "ticket planning" (also dropped the stale `.spike.md` sibling mention); `VISION.md` → "Plan tickets (aka spike)"; the dashboard package description/README → "(prototype)" instead of "(spike)".

**Identifiers** (deliberately breaking, per `AGENTS.md` zero-users policy): preset id `spike-and-plan` → `plan-tickets`, `spikeAndPlan` → `planTickets`, `SpikeAssignment` → `PlanAssignment`, `pinnedSpikeJob` → `pinnedPlanJob`, `spikeCandidates`/`lockSpikes` → `planCandidates`/`lockPlans`, and `prompts/presets/spike_and_plan.md` → `plan_tickets.md`. No migration — a config that had switched the routine off falls back to on, as the plan accepted.

**Kept, as the plan sanctioned:** the two deliberate "(aka spike)" parentheticals, historical comments (the #609 browser spike, the "#1420 folded the spike into the plan" note), changelogs/changesets, the `spike/` dev-artifacts directory, and HotTickets test names. Final grep: 12 remaining mentions, all in that sanctioned set.

**Verification:** the initial full-suite run showed 10 `daemon.test.js` failures, which turned out to be this fresh worktree missing the dashboard bundle (`test` doesn't depend on `bundle:dashboard`) — after one `pnpm run build`, everything is green with the rename in place.

```ready-for-merge
```
